preamble: Spirantization of the voiceless palatal stop [c] to the voiceless dental fricative [θ] is reconstructed for the southern branch of the Jê family. Nikulin (2020) derives Proto-Southern Jê *θ from Proto-Jê *c and assigns the change to the common Paranaense stage, since extinct Ingain also has a distinct reflex (l) of the same sound. Proto-Southern Jê *θ then became ɸ in Kaingang and ð in Laklãnõ (Xokleng), so the dental fricative itself is preserved in neither modern language.

examples.note: Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: c = voiceless palatal stop or coronal affricate, ĵ = its voiced counterpart, ñ = [ɲ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], ô/ê = close-mid vowels.

examples.to: Proto-Southern Jê *θy, verbalized *θy-n (Kaingang ɸy, Laklãnõ ðy)

examples.note: Nikulin notes that the Kaingang vowel is irregular here; the consonant correspondence is regular.

sources: Nikulin, A. (2020). Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. https://repositorio.unb.br/handle/10482/38893
